courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Observation and Assessment for Early Learning and Development (DS3)
courses.description: Introduces the appropriate use of assessment and observation tools and strategies to document young children's development and learning. The use of findings to inform and plan learning environments and experiences are emphasized. Recording strategies, rating systems, portfolios, and multiple assessment tools will be discussed along with strategies for collaboration with families and professionals. Students will be required to complete child observations in an early childhood lab school setting. CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Child, Family, and Community (DS2)
courses.description: The processes of socialization focusing on the interrelationship of family, school, and community. Examines the influence of multiple societal contexts. Explores the role of collaboration between family, community, and schools in supporting children's development, birth through adolescence. (Same as APCD 110). CSU/UC

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Principles and Practices of Teaching Young Children
courses.description: Historical contexts and theoretical perspectives of developmentally appropriate practice in early care and education for children birth through age eight. Explores the typical roles and expectations of early childhood educators. Identifies professional ethics, career pathways, and professional standards. Introduces best practices for developmentally appropriate learning environments, curriculum, and effective pedagogy for young children including how play contributes to children's learning, growth, and development. Students will be required to complete observations and assignments in an early childhood lab school setting. CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Introduction to Curriculum for Young Children
courses.description: Developmentally appropriate curriculum and environments for children birth through age eight. Students will use knowledge of children's development, theories of learning and development, and examples from various models of developmentally appropriate practice to plan environments and curriculum in all content areas to support children's development and learning integrated throughout the indoor and outdoor settings. Students will be required to complete observations and assignments in an early childhood lab school setting. CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Health, Safety, and Nutrition for Children
courses.description: Laws, regulations, standards, policies, procedures, and best practices related to health, safety, and nutrition in care and education settings for children birth through middle childhood. Includes the teacher's role in prevention strategies, nutrition and meal planning, integrating health safety and nutrition experiences into daily routines, and overall risk management. CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Careers in Teaching
courses.description: Introduction to various professional roles in teaching, student populations, career paths, academic requirements, experience levels, and credentials required for a career in teaching. Students may participate in experiential service-learning, apprenticeship, internship, or volunteer hours in various teaching environments with teacher mentors or other professionals in the education field. Students will develop an educational plan with career objectives. (Same as Counseling 114). CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Infant/Toddler Growth and Development (DS4)
courses.description: A study of infants and toddlers, from conception to 36 months, including the theoretical frameworks of development, and the impact of pregnancy, birth, and early life experiences on a child emotionally, socially, cognitively, and physically. Emphasizes the role of family, culture, caring and responsive adults, and attachment relationships on growth and development. CSU/UC

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Infant and Toddler Care and Curriculum Toddlers (DS3)
courses.description: A study of research-based approaches related to the care and education of infants and toddlers in group settings. Examines theories of learning and development, regulations, and essential practices that lead to quality care and developmentally appropriate curriculum and environments for children birth to 36 months. Emphasizes strategies to promote healthy relationships in the care and education of infants and toddlers. CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Development of the School-Age Child (DS5)
courses.description: An examination of the physical, cognitive, personality, and social development of children between the ages of five and twelve years. Attention will be paid to the scientific study of middle childhood, developmental trends, and diversity issues. Not offered every semester. (Same as Education 120A). CSU/UC

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: School-Age Child Care and Recreation Activities (DS5)
courses.description: This course will focus on school-age creative activities, including planning and implementing an appropriate before/after school curriculum. Attention will be paid to integrating academics, recreation, and creative activities suitable for school-age child care programs. (Same as Education 120B). CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Introduction to Technology in Early Childhood Education
courses.description: This course provides students with knowledge about and experience with technological tools used in early childhood settings. Students will have the opportunity to evaluate technology's impact on children's growth and development and developmentally appropriate practices. Emphasis will be on basic knowledge and practice within a wide variety of current and emerging technologies and will focus on how to integrate them into the learning environment. CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Introduction to Children With Disabilities Or Delays
courses.description: Introduces the variations in development of children and adolescents with disabilities or delay. Includes an overview of historical and societal influences, laws relating to individuals with disabilities or delays, and the assessment and referral process. Emphasizes the importance of working in partnership with families and specialists to support children's development. (Same as Education 203). CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Curriculum and Intervention Strategies For Children With Special Needs
courses.description: This covers curriculum and intervention strategies for working with children with disabilities or delays in partnership with their families. Focuses on the use of observation and assessment in meeting the individualized needs of children in inclusive and natural environments. Includes the role of the teacher as a professional working with families, collaboration with interdisciplinary teams, and cultural competence. Formerly: Curriculum and Intervention Strategies for Children with Special Needs. CSU
review: No section offering on record in CU0321; planning signal only - verify before scheduling

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Supporting and Empowering Families of Children With Special Needs
courses.description: This course will provide teachers, intervention assistants, administrators, and parents with the tools necessary to support and empower families of children with disabilities and other special needs in early childhood and school-age programs. Techniques, strategies, and resources will be provided to support children in a natural and/or inclusive educational setting and to help guide parents to be advocates of their children. CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Creative Music Experiences for Young Children
courses.description: Explores musical expression through songs and ballads, the elements of music, and diverse types of instruments as used in the early childhood curriculum. Includes the study of musical growth and development in young children and the use of music as a classroom management tool. CSU
review: No section offering on record in CU0321; planning signal only - verify before scheduling

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Creative Art Experiences for Children
courses.description: Emphasizes the child's (ages 2 through 8 years) ability to represent and expressively use art media. Includes theoretical as well as practical application and the role of adult in fostering creativity. CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Administration I: Programs in Early Childhood Education (DS6)
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the administration of early childhood programs. Students will learn about program types, budget, management, regulations, laws, development and implementation of policies and procedures. Additionally, they will examine administrative tools, philosophies, and techniques needed to organize, open, and operate an early care and education program. CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Administration II: Personnel and Leadership in Early Childhood Education (DS6)
courses.description: This course provides effective strategies for personnel management and leadership in early care and education settings. Students will learn about legal and ethical responsibilities, supervision techniques, professional development, and reflective practices for a diverse and inclusive early care and education program. CSU
review: No section offering on record in CU0321; planning signal only - verify before scheduling

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Understanding Child Abuse and Maltreatment
courses.description: Exploration of child maltreatment; this course is designed to address the correlation and potential effects from various forms of child maltreatment. Students will learn some of the possible identifying indicators of a child being maltreatment or potential factors that may be putting the child at risk. Factors such as the historical treatment of children, societal perspectives on children, family responsibilities, family dynamics and generational family dysfunction. Additionally, this course is intended to help students gain better understanding of child maltreatment and trauma in order to best support children. (Same as Counseling 220). CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Teaching in a Diverse Society
courses.description: Examines the historical and current perspectives on diversity and inclusion and the impact of systemic societal influences on children's development, learning, and school experiences. Strategies for developmentally, culturally, and linguistically appropriate anti-bias curriculum will be explored as well as approaches to promote inclusive and anti-racist classroom communities. Includes self-reflection on the influence of teachers' own culture and life experiences on teaching and interactions with children and families. (Same as APCD 221). CSU/UC

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Brain Development and Learning
courses.description: This class explores the development of the brain for children from birth through adolescence, and how behavior and learning are affected. Brain-based learning strategies will be used to teach new ways of approaching learning, including how to understand diverse learning styles. This course is designed for educators, parents, and students who are interested in knowing more about how the brain operates and how the environment affects the brain. CSU/UC
review: No section offering on record in CU0321; planning signal only - verify before scheduling

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Child Guidance and Classroom Management
courses.description: This course will define and explore developmentally appropriate expectations about young children's behavior. Students will learn the importance of the educator's knowledge about discipline strategies, effective communication skills, high-quality teacher and child interactions and the development of a skill set to address behavior issues and implement discipline strategies which are in alignment with the undesirable classroom behaviors. Behavior expectations will be defined and research-based behavioral observation skills, strategies, and assessments will be explored that best support children's various behaviors. Each student will create a community resource file of service agencies to include accessible behavior management resource materials that support teachers and students challenged with behavioral issues in the classroom. It is advised that students take this course in conjunction with working in a classroom setting. CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Developing Language and Literacy in Young Children
courses.description: Designed to introduce students to basic concepts of first and second language acquisition and literacy in young children, including classroom applications. CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Math and Science Methods for Early Learning Environments
courses.description: Introduces early childhood teachers to basic math and science principles and the standards established by the National Council of Teachers of Mathematics, the National Science Content Standards for early learning environments, the Preschool/Transitional Kindergarten Learning Foundations (PTKLF), and the Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS). This course includes theoretical and practical applications for problem-solving and critical thinking that are common in math and science curriculum. Students will develop a collection of appropriate math/science activities for early childhood environments. CSU
review: No section offering on record in CU0321; planning signal only - verify before scheduling

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Adult Supervision and Mentoring in Early Care and Education
courses.description: Methods and principles of supervising, mentoring, and coaching student teachers and other adults in early care and education settings. Presents the strategies and skills necessary to support the development of adult learners as effective mentors, coaches, and teachers. Emphasis is on individualized, relationship- and strengths-based approaches, reflective practices, and constructive communication skills. Covers characteristics and roles, career requirements and pathways, and use of evaluation in setting professional learning goals. CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Practicum - Student Teaching Field Experience
courses.description: Demonstration of developmentally appropriate early childhood program planning and teaching competencies under the supervision of CDES faculty and other qualified early education professionals. Students will utilize practical classroom experiences to make connections between theory and practice, develop professional behaviors, and build a comprehensive understanding of children and families. Reflective practice will be emphasized as student teachers design, implement, and evaluate approaches, strategies, and techniques that promote development and learning. Includes exploration of career pathways, professional development, and teacher responsibilities. Students are required to complete a minimum of 108 hours in an early childhood lab school setting or approved mentor site. CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Analyzing and Applying Teacher Strategies in the Classroom
courses.description: This course prepares pre-service early childhood and early elementary education teachers to effectively use formative and summative assessments to understand and support the developmental, academic, and social-emotional progress of young children in Preschool-Third Grade classrooms. Candidates will learn to use assessment data to inform instruction that is developmentally appropriate, intentional, and aligned with content standards. The course emphasizes the design of inclusive learning environments that integrate Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles and apply a Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS) framework to address diverse learner needs. Special attention will be given to culturally and linguistically responsive teaching practices, strategies for supporting English learners, and building strong partnerships with families. Students are required to complete 25 hours of structured observation and fieldwork experience in an approved early childhood and/or elementary school classroom setting. CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Work Experience - Child Development
courses.description: This work experience course of supervised employment is designed to assist students to acquire career awareness and work habits in early childhood, PK-12, and after-school programs. 54 hours of work equals one unit of course credit. Student repetition is allowed per Title 5, Section 55253. Students may earn a maximum of 14 units of credit for work experience. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only. Open Entry/Open Exit. CSU

courses.subject: CDEV
courses.title: Child Growth and Development
courses.description: Students examine the progression of development in the physical, cognitive, social, and emotional domains and identify developmental milestones for children from conception through adolescence. Emphasis is on interactions between biological processes, environmental, and cultural factors. Students may engage in various methods of observing children's development to evaluate individual differences and analyze development characteristics at various stages according to developmental theories. A student will not receive credit for this course if they have already taken Psychology 157. Formerly: CDEV 107 - Child Growth and Development (DS1). CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Exploration in the Field of Education
courses.description: An exploration in the field of education from early childhood through high school. This course requires 15 hours of structured observation in traditional and non-traditional settings: early childhood, elementary school, middle school, high school, special education, and English Language Development (ELD). Topics will include: a) roles and responsibilities of the teacher, b) teaching and learning of diverse student populations across different education spans, and c) careers in education beyond the classroom teacher. CSU

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Tutoring Reading in Elementary Schools
courses.description: An examination of effective tutoring strategies focusing on supporting reading skills of elementary-age children. Students will independently complete a minimum of twenty hours of service learning (tutoring of TK-8th students in home and/or school settings) in addition to lecture hours. CSU

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Development of the School-Age Child
courses.description: An examination of the physical, cognitive, personality, and social development of children between the ages of five and twelve years. Attention will be paid to the scientific study of middle childhood, developmental trends, and diversity issues. Not offered every semester. (Same as Child Development 120A). CSU/UC

Attention will be paid to integrating academics, recreation, and creative activities suitable for school-age child care programs. (Same as Child Development 120B). CSU

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Introduction to Elementary Classroom Teaching
courses.description: Introduces students to the concepts and issues related to teaching diverse learners in today's contemporary schools, kindergarten through grade 12 (K-12). Topics include teaching as a profession and career, historical and philosophical foundations of the American education system, contemporary educational issues, California's content standards and frameworks, and teacher performance standards. In addition to class time, the course requires a minimum of 45 hours of structured fieldwork in public school elementary classrooms that represent California's diverse student population, and includes cooperation with at least one approved certificated classroom teacher. CSU/UC

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Introduction to Children With Disabilities Or Delays
courses.description: Introduces the variations in development of children and adolescents with disabilities or delay. Includes an overview of historical and societal influences, laws relating to individuals with disabilities or delays, and the assessment and referral process. Emphasizes the importance of working in partnership with families and specialists to support children's development. (Same as Child Development 205). CSU

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Proficiency in Educational Technologies For Teachers
courses.description: Students will develop personal proficiency in educational technologies to facilitate the teaching process. Students will also apply digital literacy skills through the use of presentation, spreadsheet, word processing and publication software, interactive online tools, internet search and retrieval, information literacy, electronic communication and collaboration, and awareness of legal and ethical issues in the digital world. CSU

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: The Teaching Experience: Secondary Education
courses.description: Introduction to the history, philosophy, and sociology of secondary education. This course will cover the California Teaching Performance Expectation and Assessment, needs of students with disabilities, English learners, struggling readers, content standards, and major curriculum reform documents. Students participate in 45 hours of structured observation in a local secondary classroom. CSU/UC

notes: CU0002 is parsed explicitly; unrecognized catalog layouts are not guessed.
Crosswalk ownership is college-aware; ambiguous ownership remains flagged instead of silently assigned.
CU0321 last-offered data is a planning signal only and does not determine curriculum currency.
DO NOT SCHEDULE rooms are owner-only when a matching owner division is present; they are not campuswide rooms.
Shared portal writes are revalidated server-side; browser-calculated totals are not trusted.
Local database mode writes proposals to SQLite with revision history and stores per-department draft workspaces; static HTML is preview-only for database actions.
Department draft workspaces are isolated by term/college/division/department so switching scope does not destroy unfinished work.
2026-27 credit default is Standardized Attendance Accounting; open-entry/open-exit credit remains Actual Hours / Positive Attendance.
Faculty load caps/factors are configurable planning values, not a contractual certification.
Pathway membership comes only from a confirmed administrator-provided mapping; it is never inferred from course title, TOP code, or division.
Imported existing bookings are a snapshot at generation time, not a live Ad Astra/Colleague connection; regenerate after refreshing the booking export.
Empty optional booking/pathway CSV files are ignored with import warnings; malformed or headerless files produce a clear validation error instead of a raw csv traceback.
RG0547 prepopulation maps prior dates by relative term week + weekday; previous CRNs are retained only as a reference and are never reused as current-term identifiers.
Block schedule alignment is advisory. The planner suggests approved windows and permits documented exceptions rather than blocking CTE/long-format schedules.
Department-chair modality labels are translated to scheduler/Colleague codes from the imported DE coding reference when available.
